issues.failure_explanation: Since Cl'(θ) = −log|2 sin(θ/2)| ≈ −log θ near 0, the difference quotient (Cl(x+ε)−Cl(x))/ε is asymptotic to −log x, not +log x. Taking x→0+ with fixed small ε, the left side of the first displayed inequality grows like 2|log x| while the right-hand bound ½ε/x + log(2/π) stays < 0 (log(2/π) ≈ −0.45), so the first inequality is violated for all small x. In the second displayed estimate the main term −log(2π−x) is correct, but at x = π+ε the true error tends to log(π/2) ≈ 0.45 > 0, so the claimed bound ½ε/(2π−x) + log(2/π) (which is negative for small ε) cannot hold. Both estimates in item 6 are false as displayed; the logarithmic main term has the wrong sign (or equivalently the constant has the wrong sign).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct item 6 by flipping the sign of the logarithmic main terms (the estimates must compare with −log x and with +log(2π−x) respectively) and replacing log(2/π) by log(2/π)→log(π/2); re-derive the two bounds from Cl'(θ) = −log(2 sin(θ/2)) with the standard split of the integral. This is a local, routine correction; no downstream result uses the first estimate and a38's second-branch use only needs O(1) quality, which the corrected bounds still provide.
issues.overall_effect: Item 6 of Proposition a24 is asserted as a 'standard result' but is false; any argument importing these finite-difference estimates for the Clausen function (e.g. step 6-type estimates feeding into Lemma a38's second branch) is unsupported as written. The estimates are not load-bearing enough in the regimes used to invalidate later results, but the proposition itself is defective.
issues.title: Proposition's Clausen finite-difference estimates (item 6) are false
issues.why_classification: Both erroneous inequalities are localized recalled estimates; replacing them with correctly signed versions (main term −log x in the first, positive constant log(π/2) in the second) is a routine repair, and no labelled downstream result depends on the false versions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In addition, by \Cref{a24}, $\Cl(\eps n/2) = \hat C \alpha(1-\alpha) \log (2/\alpha)$ for some $\hat C \in [1/\pi,2/5]$.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed assertion in item 7 claims Cl(απ)/(α(1−α)log(2/α)) ∈ [1/π, 2/5]. At α = 1/2, Cl(π/2) = G ≈ 0.916 and α(1−α)log(2/α) = ¼·log 4 ≈ 0.3466, giving ratio ≈ 2.64, far outside [0.318, 0.40]. The correct statement is the reciprocal: (α(1−α)log(2/α))/Cl(απ) ∈ [1/π, 2/5]. The proposition supplies no proof (it is recalled as 'standard'), and the only labelled use (Lemma a30) inherits a wrong constant range, though only constants are at stake there.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed inclusion by the equivalent inverted one, (α(1−α) log(2/α))/Cl(απ) ∈ [1/π, 2/5] (equivalently Cl(απ)/(α(1−α)log(2/α)) ∈ [2/5, π]), and update the constant range quoted in Lemma a30; all downstream conclusions are unchanged up to constants.
issues.overall_effect: The recalled constant range in Proposition a24, item 7, is false; Lemma a30's quoted constant range for Ĉ is wrong, but a30's conclusion M_n/M_w ≍ log(2/α) survives with adjusted constants, so no downstream labelled result fails.
issues.title: Catalan-ratio range in Proposition item 7 is inverted
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local swap of the ratio (equivalently inverting the interval), affects only a constant range, and no subsequent result depends on the specific numerical constants; the qualitative estimate Cl(απ) ≍ α(1−α)log(2/α) remains true.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines Disk(z,r) = {w : |w−z| ≤ r} (closed disks) and uses these closed disks in the definition of the KS distance. The point z_+ need not be a node, and r := dist(z_+, S) > 0 is the distance to the nearest node, so the closed ball Disk(z_+, r) contains the nearest node z_k on its boundary; hence μ_S(Disk(z_+, r)) ≥ 1/(n+1) > 0, contradicting the claimed 'μ_S(Disk(z_+, dist(z_+, S))) = 0'. Consequently the inferred inequality KS(μ, μ_S) ≥ μ(Disk(z_+, r)) ≥ ρ₂ r^β is not justified as written; the correct deduction only gives KS(μ, μ_S) ≥ ρ₂ r^β − 1/(n+1). The same issue affects the proof of Lemma a50's second inequality, where the bound dist(z_+,S)^α ≤ O(ks(μ_S,μ)^{α/β}) is obtained from this step: as written one only gets dist(z_+,S)^α ≤ O((ks(μ_S,μ) + 1/(n+1))^{α/β}), and the additional n^{−α/β}-type error is not absorbed by the error terms displayed in Theorem a10 without a further (routine) argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the closed ball by the open ball Disk°(z_+, dist(z_+,S)), for which μ_S vanishes, and use the KS distance restricted to open balls together with condition (3) and a limiting argument (or insert the harmless extra term O(1/(n+1)^{α/β}) ≪ (log n)/n into the error); either way Theorem a10's displayed estimate remains true with a marginally enlarged O(·) term.
issues.overall_effect: The lower-bound half of Lemma a50 (and hence the two-sided asymptotic in Theorem a10) rests on an invalid step as written; the range(U^μ) lower estimate and the error terms in Theorem a10 are not established by the printed argument, although a routine repair (using the open ball, or combining ks(μ,μ_S) ≥ 1/(2(n+1)) with the ρ₂-bound) restores an equivalent statement.
issues.title: Lemma a50 claims μ_S of the ball around z_+ is zero, false for the paper's closed disks
issues.why_classification: The gap is local: the same quantity can be bounded below by ρ₂ dist^β minus the single atom mass 1/(n+1), and since the Lemma's own triangle-inequality step shows ks(μ_S, μ) ≥ 1/(n+1), the desired estimate dist(z_+,S)^α = O(ks^{α/β}) is recovered by a routine, purely local modification; no rate or guarantee is lost.
